'''Gráda''' is a traditional [[Irish music]] band founded in 2001 whose members are a mix of Irish and New Zealand musicians. Based in Dublin and Galway, Ireland, Gráda have spent much of their time touring internationally.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.womex.com/virtual/strada_music/grada | title=Grada - WOMEX }}</ref> In 2011, members of Gráda disbanded to work on individual projects.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gradamusic.com/info.html|title = Info}}</ref> The band reformed in 2020 to play a concert in New Zealand and were joined by Tola Custy.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.eventfinda.co.nz/2020/gardens-magic-2020-grada-pauline-scanlon-band/wellington | title=Gardens Magic 2020 - Gráda/Pauline Scanlon Band }}</ref> In October 2023 they reformed to embark on a nine date tour of New Zealand, to be followed by dates in Ireland<ref>https://www.gradamusic.ie/</ref>

==Musical career==
The group draws from a wide range of influences, which has seen them working with Dave Hingerty ([[Kíla]], [[The Frames]], [[The Swell Season]]); Vyviene Long (cellist with [[Damien Rice]]); and, as a producer, Trevor Hutchinson (Lúnasa, Sharon Shannon, The Waterboys). Further additions have included Dublin based trumpeter Bill Blackmore and percussionist Rasmus Skovmand.

In 2008, it was announced Colin Farrell had decided to leave the band. He was replaced by multi-instrumentalist David Doocey.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.allcelticmusic.com/artists/David%20Doocey.html | title=David Doocey }}</ref> In April 2009, Alan Doherty left the band and was replaced by Stephen Doherty (no relation). Alan returned to the group in 2011.

==Charts and critical reception==
Gráda have received critical acclaim, with their latest album ''Natural Angle'' being voted as one of the top folk albums of 2010 in the USA by NPR / Folk Alley and the IMA music awards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://compassrecords.com/news.php?story=735 |title=Compass Records |access-date=26 November 2011 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130119153900/http://compassrecords.com/news.php?story=735 |archive-date=19 January 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Their previous album, ''Cloudy Day Navigation'' appeared multiple times in ''[[Irish Music (magazine)|Irish Music]]'s'' Top 10 charts.<ref>Irish Music Magazine.
